title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 88 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 486–489 (Night 88, continuing directly from nights-87), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 88 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Sharrukān and Ḍawʾ al-Makān set out with the armies of Islam for the land of Rūm, while the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī and the kings of Rūm and Constantinople gather the Christian host and the Franks. The two armies meet in the valley by the salt sea, the vizier Dandān rides out first, and the old woman promises her king a plan even Iblīs could not devise, until dawn cuts Shahrazād off. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّامِنَةُ وَالثَّمَانُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thāminatu wa-al-thamānūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the eighth and the eighty,
sentences.i: And when it was the eighty-eighth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدَأَنَّ شَرْكَانَ قَالَ لِأَخِيهِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ أَمَا كَافَأْتَ الْوَقَّادَ عَلَى مَعْرُوفِهِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīda anna sharrukāna qāla li-akhīhi ḍawʾi al-makāni amā kāfaʾta al-waqqāda ʿalā maʿrūfihi
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that Sharrukān said to his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān: Have you not rewarded the stoker for his kindness?
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that Sharrukān said to his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān: “Have you not yet repaid the stoker for his kindness?”
sentences.n: The print runs أن (“that”) into the word before it (السعيدان, “the happy — that”); it is read as two words, and the spacing is kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا أَخِي مَا كَافَئْتُهُ إِلَى الْآنَ وَلَكِنْ أُكَافِئُهُ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى لَمَّا أَرْجِعُ مِنَ الْغَزْوَةِ وَأَتَفَرَّغُ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yā akhī mā kāfaʾtuhu ilā al-āna wa-lākin ukāfiʾuhu in shāʾa allāhu taʿālā lammā arjiʿu mina al-ghazwati wa-atafarraghu lahu
sentences.l: And he said to him: O my brother, I have not rewarded him up to now, but I will reward him, if God the Exalted wills, when I return from the raid and empty myself for him.
sentences.i: He answered: “My brother, I have not repaid him until now, but I will, God willing, when I come back from the campaign and have leisure for it.”
sentences.n: The print writes the verb as كافئته, with the hamza on a yāʾ-seat; it is the same كافأته, “I rewarded him”.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ عَرَفَ شَرْكَانُ أَنَّ أُخْتَهُ الْمَلِكَةَ نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ صَادِقَةٌ فِي جَمِيعِ مَا أَخْبَرَتْهُ بِهِ ثُمَّ كَتَمَ أَمْرَهُ وَأَمْرَهَا وَأَرْسَلَ إِلَيْهَا السَّلَامَ مَعَ الْحَاجِبِ زَوْجِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika ʿarafa sharrukānu anna ukhtahu al-malikata nuzhata al-zamāni ṣādiqatun fī jamīʿi mā akhbaratuhu bihi thumma katama amrahu wa-amrahā wa-arsala ilayhā al-salāma maʿa al-ḥājibi zawjihā
sentences.l: So at that Sharrukān knew that his sister the queen Nuzhat al-Zamān was truthful in all that she had told him; then he hid his affair and her affair, and sent to her the greeting with the chamberlain, her husband.
sentences.i: At that Sharrukān knew that his sister, Queen Nuzhat al-Zamān, had told him the truth in everything; then he kept his own business and hers secret, and sent her his greetings by the chamberlain, her husband.

sentences.t: فَبَعَثَتْ لَهُ أَيْضًا مَعَهُ السَّلَامَ وَدَعَتْ لَهُ وَسَأَلَتْ عَنِ ابْنَتِهَا قَضَى فَكَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-baʿathat lahu ayḍan maʿahu al-salāma wa-daʿat lahu wa-saʾalat ʿani ibnatihā qaḍā fakāna
sentences.l: And she sent him also, with him, the greeting, and prayed for him, and asked about her daughter Qaḍā Fakān.
sentences.i: She sent him greetings in return by the same man, and prayed for him, and asked after her daughter, Qaḍā Fakān.
sentences.n: قضى فكان (“what was decreed came to be”) is the daughter’s name; it is a phrase, kept as the print gives it. ابنة, “daughter”, is the print’s word here.

sentences.t: فَأَخْبَرَهَا أَنَّهَا فِي عَافِيَةٍ وَأَنَّهَا فِي غَايَةِ مَا يَكُونُ مِنَ الصِّحَّةِ وَالسَّلَامَةِ فَحَمِدَتِ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى وَشَكَرَتْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-akhbarahā annahā fī ʿāfiyatin wa-annahā fī ghāyati mā yakūnu mina al-ṣiḥḥati wa-al-salāmati fa-ḥamidati allāha taʿālā wa-shakaratuhu
sentences.l: And he told her that she was in well-being, and that she was at the utmost of what is of health and safety; and she praised God the Exalted and thanked him.
sentences.i: He told her that the girl was well and in the best of health and safety, and she praised God the Exalted and thanked him.

sentences.t: وَرَجَعَ شَرْكَانُ إِلَى أَخِيهِ يُشَاوِرُهُ فِي أَمْرِ الرَّحِيلِ
sentences.tr: wa-rajaʿa sharrukānu ilā akhīhi yushāwiruhu fī amri al-raḥīli
sentences.l: And Sharrukān returned to his brother, consulting him in the matter of the departure.
sentences.i: Sharrukān went back to his brother to consult him about setting out.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا أَخِي لَمَّا تَتَكَامَلُ الْعَسَاكِرُ وَتَأَنَّى الْعُرْبَانُ مِنْ كُلِّ مَكَانٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yā akhī lammā tatakāmalu al-ʿasākiru wa-taʾannā al-ʿurbānu min kulli makānin
sentences.l: And he said to him: O my brother, when the armies are completed, and the Bedouin have waited, from every place —
sentences.i: He said to him: “My brother, when the armies are complete and the Bedouin have gathered from every quarter —”
sentences.n: The print has وتانى, which can only be read as تأنّى, “took its time, waited”; the sense wants “came” (perhaps وتأتي). Kept as printed, vocalised as the letters allow. The speech breaks off without its main clause, and the next sentence begins with ثم.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِتَجْهِيزِ الْمِيرَةِ وَإِحْضَارِ الذَّخِيرَةِ وَدَخَلَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ إِلَى زَوْجَتِهِ وَكَانَ مَضَى لَهَا خَمْسَةُ أَشْهُرٍ
sentences.tr: thumma amara bi-tajhīzi al-mīrati wa-iḥḍāri al-dhakhīrati wa-dakhala ḍawʾu al-makāni ilā zawjatihi wa-kāna maḍā lahā khamsatu ashhurin
sentences.l: Then he commanded the equipping of the provisions and the bringing of the stores, and Ḍawʾ al-Makān went in to his wife, and five months had passed for her.
sentences.i: Then he ordered provisions to be made ready and supplies brought in, and Ḍawʾ al-Makān went in to his wife, who had been five months along.
sentences.n: The print does not say five months of what; the sense is almost certainly her pregnancy, and the English says so.

sentences.t: وَجَعَلَ أَرْبَابَ الْأَقْلَامِ وَأَهْلَ الْحِسَابِ تَحْتَ طَاعَتِهَا وَرَتَّبَ لَهُمُ الْجَرَايَاتِ وَالْجَوَامِكَ وَسَافَرَ فِي ثَالِثِ شَهْرٍ مِنْ حِينِ نُزُولِ عَسْكَرِ الشَّامِ بَعْدَ أَنْ قَدِمَتِ الْعُرْبَانُ وَجَمِيعُ الْعَسَاكِرِ مِنْ كُلِّ مَكَانٍ
sentences.tr: wa-jaʿala arbāba al-aqlāmi wa-ahla al-ḥisābi taḥta ṭāʿatihā wa-rattaba lahumu al-jarāyāti wa-al-jawāmika wa-sāfara fī thālithi shahrin min ḥīni nuzūli ʿaskari al-shāmi baʿda an qadimati al-ʿurbānu wa-jamīʿu al-ʿasākiri min kulli makānin
sentences.l: And he made the lords of the pens and the people of the reckoning under her obedience, and arranged for them the allowances and the stipends, and travelled in the third month from the time of the descent of the army of Syria, after the Bedouin had arrived, and all the armies, from every place.
sentences.i: He put the scribes and the men of accounts under her authority and fixed their rations and salaries, and set out in the third month after the Syrian army had come down, once the Bedouin and all the other troops had arrived from every quarter.
sentences.n: “Lords of the pens” are the scribes and secretaries of the treasury and chancery.

sentences.t: وَسَارَتِ الْجُيُوشُ وَالْعَسَاكِرُ وَتَتَابَعَتِ الْجَحَافِلُ وَكَانَ اسْمُ رَئِيسِ عَسْكَرِ الدَّيْلَمِ رُسْتُمَ وَاسْمُ رَئِيسِ عَسْكَرِ التُّرْكِ بَهْرَمَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-sārati al-juyūshu wa-al-ʿasākiru wa-tatābaʿati al-jaḥāfilu wa-kāna ismu raʾīsi ʿaskari al-daylami rustama wa-ismu raʾīsi ʿaskari al-turki bahramāna
sentences.l: And the hosts and the armies went, and the great-columns followed one upon another; and the name of the head of the army of the Daylam was Rustam, and the name of the head of the army of the Turks was Bahramān.
sentences.i: The hosts and armies marched, column following column; the commander of the Daylamite troops was named Rustam, and the commander of the Turks Bahramān.
sentences.n: The Daylam are the highland people of northern Iran, long famed as soldiers.

sentences.t: وَصَارَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ فِي وَسَطِ الْجُيُوشِ وَعَنْ يَمِينِهِ أَخُوهُ شَرْكَانُ وَعَنْ يَسَارِهِ الْحَاجِبُ صِهْرُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra ḍawʾu al-makāni fī wasaṭi al-juyūshi wa-ʿan yamīnihi akhūhu sharrukānu wa-ʿan yasārihi al-ḥājibu ṣihruhu
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān was in the middle of the hosts, and on his right his brother Sharrukān, and on his left the chamberlain, his son-in-law.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān rode in the middle of the hosts, with his brother Sharrukān on his right and the chamberlain, his brother-in-law, on his left.
sentences.n: The print has اخوة (“brothers”), a misprint for اخوه (“his brother”), corrected here. صهر covers any relative by marriage; the chamberlain is Nuzhat al-Zamān’s husband, so to Ḍawʾ al-Makān he is a brother-in-law.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا سَائِرِينَ مُدَّةَ شَهْرٍ وَكُلَّ جُمْعَةٍ يَنْزِلُونَ فِي مَكَانٍ وَيَسْتَرِيحُونَ فِيهِ ثَلْثَةَ أَيَّامٍ لِأَنَّ الْخَلْقَ كَثِيرٌ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazālū sā’irīna muddata shahrin wa-kulla jumʿatin yanzilūna fī makānin wa-yastarīḥūna fīhi thalthata ayyāmin li-anna al-khalqa kathīrun
sentences.l: And they did not cease travelling for the length of a month, and every week they alighted in a place and rested in it three days, because the creation was many.
sentences.i: They went on travelling for a month, and every week they camped somewhere and rested there three days, because the host was so great.
sentences.n: جمعة here is “week” (the Friday cycle), not Friday. خلق, “creation”, is used for “the people, the crowd”. ثلثة is the edition’s spelling of ثلاثة.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَٰلُوا سَائِرِينَ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْحَالَةِ حَتَّى وَصَلُوا إِلَى بِلَادِ الرُّومِ فَنَفَرَتْ أَهْلُ الْقُرَى وَالضِّيَاعِ وَالصَّعَا لِيكِ وَفَرُّوا إِلَى الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazalū sā’irīna ʿalā hādhihi al-ḥālati ḥattā waṣalū ilā bilādi al-rūmi fa-nafarat ahlu al-qurā wa-al-ḍiyāʿi wa-al-ṣaʿā līki wa-farrū ilā al-qusṭanṭīniyyati
sentences.l: And they did not cease travelling in this state until they reached the lands of Rūm, and the people of the villages and the estates and the vagabonds took fright, and fled to Constantinople.
sentences.i: They went on in this way until they reached the lands of Rūm, and the people of the villages, the estates and the open country took fright and fled to Constantinople.
sentences.n: The print writes يزلوا without the long ā (read here with a dagger alif), and splits الصعاليك, “the vagabonds, the poor”, into الصعا and ليك; the spacing is kept as printed. Rūm is the Byzantine, Christian north.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ أَفْرِيدُونُ مَلِكُهُمْ بِخَبَرِهِمْ قَامَ وَتَوَجَّهَ إِلَى ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa afrīdūnu malikuhum bi-khabarihim qāma wa-tawajjaha ilā dhāti al-dawāhī
sentences.l: And when Afrīdūn their king heard of their news, he arose and went toward Dhāt al-Dawāhī,
sentences.i: When Afrīdūn, their king, heard the news of them, he rose and went to Dhāt al-Dawāhī,

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهَا هِيَ الَّتِي دَبَّرَتِ الْحِيَلَ وَسَافَرَتْ إِلَى بَغْدَادَ حَتَّى قَتَلَتِ الْمَلِكَ عُمَرَ بْنَ النُّعْمَانِ ثُمَّ أَخَذَتْ جَوَارِيَهَا وَالْمَلِكَةَ صَفِيَّةَ وَرَجَعَتْ بِالْجَمِيعِ إِلَى بِلَادِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-innahā hiya allatī dabbarati al-ḥiyala wa-sāfarat ilā baghdāda ḥattā qatalati al-malika ʿumara bna al-nuʿmāni thumma akhadhat jawāriyahā wa-al-malikata ṣafiyyata wa-rajaʿat bi-al-jamīʿi ilā bilādihā
sentences.l: for she, she is the one who contrived the stratagems and travelled to Baghdad until she killed the king ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān; then she took her slave-girls and the queen Ṣafiyya, and returned with all of them to her lands.
sentences.i: for it was she who had contrived the plots and travelled to Baghdad until she killed King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān; then she had taken her slave-girls and Queen Ṣafiyya and gone back with them all to her own country.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَجَعَتْ إِلَى وَلَدِهَا مَلِكِ الرُّومِ وَأَمِنَتْ عَلَى نَفْسِهَا قَالَتْ لِا بْنِهَا قَرَّعَيْنًا فَقَدْ أَخَذْتُ لَكَ بِثَأْرِ ابْنَتِكَ أَبْرِيزَةَ وَقَتَلْتُ الْمَلِكَ عُمَرَ بْنَ النُّعْمَانِ وَجِئْتُ بِصَفِيَّةَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā rajaʿat ilā waladihā maliki al-rūmi wa-aminat ʿalā nafsihā qālat li-ibnihā qarra ʿaynan fa-qad akhadhtu laka bi-thaʾri ibnatika abrīzata wa-qataltu al-malika ʿumara bna al-nuʿmāni wa-jiʾtu bi-ṣafiyyata
sentences.l: And when she returned to her son the king of Rūm, and was safe for herself, she said to her son: Be cool of eye! For I have taken for you the blood-revenge of your daughter Abrīza, and I killed the king ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, and I came with Ṣafiyya.
sentences.i: When she came back to her son, the king of Rūm, and felt safe, she said to him: “Rest content! I have taken vengeance for your daughter Abrīza, killed King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, and brought Ṣafiyya back.
sentences.n: قرّعينا is قرّ عينًا, “may your eye be cool”, that is, be glad; the print sets it as one word (with its shadda) and splits لابنها as لا بنها, and the spacing is kept as printed. The “son” is Ḥardūb, king of Rūm, so Abrīza is his daughter.

sentences.t: فَقُمِ الْآنَ وَارْحَلْ إِلَى مَلِكِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ وَرُدَّ عَلَيْهِ صَفِيَّةَ ابْنَتَهُ وَأَعْلِمْهُ بِمَا جَرَى حَتَّى يَكُونَ جَمِيعُنَا عَلَى حَذَرٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qumi al-āna wa-irḥal ilā maliki al-qusṭanṭīniyyati wa-rudda ʿalayhi ṣafiyyata ibnatahu wa-aʿlimhu bi-mā jarā ḥattā yakūna jamīʿunā ʿalā ḥadharin
sentences.l: So arise now, and set out to the king of Constantinople, and return to him Ṣafiyya his daughter, and let him know what has happened, until all of us are on guard,
sentences.i: So get up now and go to the king of Constantinople, give his daughter Ṣafiyya back to him, and tell him all that has happened, so that we are all on our guard,

sentences.t: وَنَتَجَهَّزَ بِأُهْبَةٍ وَأُسَافِرَأَنَا مَعَكَ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ مَلِكِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ وَأَظُنُّ أَنَّ الْمُسْلِمِينَ لَا يَثْبُتُونَ عَلَى قِتَالِنَا
sentences.tr: wa-natajahhaza bi-uhbatin wa-usāfira anā maʿaka ilā al-maliki afrīdūna maliki al-qusṭanṭīniyyati wa-aẓunnu anna al-muslimīna lā yathbutūna ʿalā qitālinā
sentences.l: and we equip ourselves with readiness, and I travel, I, with you to the king Afrīdūn, king of Constantinople; and I think that the Muslims will not stand firm against our fighting.
sentences.i: and make ready in full order; and I shall travel with you to King Afrīdūn of Constantinople. I think the Muslims will not be able to stand against us in battle.”
sentences.n: The print runs وأسافر and أنا together (وأسافرانا); the spacing is kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا أَمْهِلِي إِلَى أَنْ يَقْرُبُوا مِنْ بِلَادِنَا حَتَّى نُجَهِّزَ أَحْوَالَنَا ثُمَّ أَخَذُوا فِي جَمْعِ رِجَالِهِمْ وَتَجْهِيزِ أَحَدُوا لَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā amhilī ilā an yaqrubū min bilādinā ḥattā nujahhiza aḥwālanā thumma akhadhū fī jamʿi rijālihim wa-tajhīzi aḥadū lahum
sentences.l: And he said to her: Give respite until they draw near to our lands, until we equip our affairs. Then they began in the gathering of their men and the equipping of “aḥadū” for them.
sentences.i: He said to her: “Wait until they come closer to our country, so that we can make our preparations.” Then they set about gathering their men and equipping …
sentences.n: أحدوا لهم is obscure and probably corrupt (perhaps احوالهم, “their affairs”, which the next sentence echoes with حالهم); kept as printed, and the English breaks off.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمُ الْخَبَرُ كَانُوا قَدْ جَهَّزُوا حَالَهُمْ وَجَمَعُوا الْجُيُوشَ وَسَارَتْ فِي أَوَائِلِهِمْ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā jāʾahumu al-khabaru kānū qad jahhazū ḥālahum wa-jamaʿū al-juyūsha wa-sārat fī awāʾilihim dhātu al-dawāhī
sentences.l: And when the news came to them, they had equipped their state and gathered the hosts, and Dhāt al-Dawāhī went among the first of them.
sentences.i: By the time the news reached them they were ready and had gathered their armies, and Dhāt al-Dawāhī rode among the foremost.
sentences.n: The print has الدوهي, a misprint for الدواهي, corrected here.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلُوا الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةَ سَمِعَ الْمَلِكُ الْأَكْبَرُ مَلِكُهَا أَفْرِيدُونُ بِقُدُومِ حَرْدُوبَ مَلِكِ الرُّومِ فَخَرَجَ لِمُلَاقَاتِهِ فَلَمَّا اجْتَمَعَ أَفْرِيدُونُ بِمَلِكِ الرُّومِ سَأَلَهُ عَنْ حَالِهِ وَعَنْ سَبَبِ قُدُومِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣalū al-qusṭanṭīniyyata samiʿa al-maliku al-akbaru malikuhā afrīdūnu bi-qudūmi ḥardūba maliki al-rūmi fa-kharaja li-mulāqātihi fa-lammā ijtamaʿa afrīdūnu bi-maliki al-rūmi saʾalahu ʿan ḥālihi wa-ʿan sababi qudūmihi
sentences.l: And when they reached Constantinople, the greatest king, its king Afrīdūn, heard of the coming of Ḥardūb king of Rūm, and went out to meet him; and when Afrīdūn met with the king of Rūm he asked him about his state and about the cause of his coming.
sentences.i: When they reached Constantinople, the Great King, Afrīdūn, its ruler, heard that Ḥardūb, king of Rūm, had arrived and went out to meet him; and when they were together he asked him how he was and what had brought him.

sentences.t: فَأَخْبَرَهُ بِمَا عَمِلَتْهُ أَنَّهُ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي مِنَ الْحِيَلِ وَأَنَّهَا قَتَلَتْ مَلِكَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَأَخَذَتْ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ الْمَلِكَةَ صَفِيَّةَ
sentences.tr: fa-akhbarahu bi-mā ʿamilathu annahu dhātu al-dawāhī mina al-ḥiyali wa-annahā qatalat malika al-muslimīna wa-akhadhat min ʿindihi al-malikata ṣafiyyata
sentences.l: And he told him of what she had done — that she, Dhāt al-Dawāhī, of the stratagems — and that she had killed the king of the Muslims and taken from his house the queen Ṣafiyya,
sentences.i: He told him what she had done: how, by her cunning, she had killed the king of the Muslims and taken Queen Ṣafiyya from his court,
sentences.n: The print has انه (“that he”) before ذات الدواهي; it is kept as printed and read loosely, as “that she, Dhāt al-Dawāhī, [had acted] by stratagems”. The Arabic here is awkward and may be slightly corrupt.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ إِنَّ الْمُسْلِمِينَ جَمَعُوا عَسَاكِرَهُمْ وَجَاؤُا وَنُرِيدَأَنْ نَكُونَ جَمِيعُنَا يَدًا وَاحِدَةً وَنَلْقَاهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat inna al-muslimīna jamaʿū ʿasākirahum wa-jāʾū wa-nurīda an nakūna jamīʿunā yadan wāḥidatan wa-nalqāhum
sentences.l: and she said that the Muslims had gathered their armies and come, and we want that we be, all of us, one hand, and meet them.
sentences.i: and she had said that the Muslims had gathered their armies and were coming, and that we must all be one hand and meet them.
sentences.n: The print runs ونريد and ان together (ونريدان); the spacing is kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ الْمَلِكُ أَفْرِيدُونُ بِقُدُومِ ابْنَتِهِ وَقَتْلِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ وَأَرْسَلَ إِلَى سَائِرِ الْأَقَالِيمِ يَطْلُبُ مِنْهُ النَّجْدَةَ وَيَذْكُرُ لَهُمْ سَبَبَ قَتْلِ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa al-maliku afrīdūnu bi-qudūmi ibnatihi wa-qatli ʿumara bni al-nuʿmāni wa-arsala ilā sāʾiri al-aqālīmi yaṭlubu minhu al-najdata wa-yadhkuru lahum sababa qatli al-maliki ʿumara bni al-nuʿmāni
sentences.l: And the king Afrīdūn rejoiced at the coming of his daughter and the killing of ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, and sent to all the regions, asking of him help, and mentioning to them the cause of the killing of the king ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān.
sentences.i: King Afrīdūn rejoiced that his daughter had come home and that ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān was dead, and he sent to all the regions asking for help and telling them why King ʿUmar had been killed.
sentences.n: The print has النمعان, a misprint for النعمان, corrected here (the same name is spelled correctly further on in this night). يطلب منه is singular in the print, though the regions are many.

sentences.t: فَهَرَعَتْ إِلَيْهِ جُيُوشُ النَّصَارَى فَمَامَرَّ ثَلْثَةُ شُهُورٍ حَتَّى تَكَامَلَتْ جُيُوشُ الرُّومِ
sentences.tr: fa-haraʿat ilayhi juyūshu al-naṣārā fa-mā marra thalthatu shuhūrin ḥattā takāmalat juyūshu al-rūmi
sentences.l: And the hosts of the Christians hurried to him, and three months did not pass until the hosts of Rūm were complete.
sentences.i: The Christian armies hurried to him, and three months had not passed before the armies of Rūm were all assembled.
sentences.n: The print runs فما and مر together (فمامر); the spacing is kept as printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَتِ الْإِفْرَنْجُ مِنْ سَائِرِ أَطْرَافِهَا كَا لْفَرْ نَسِيسِ وَالنَّمْسَا وَدُوبَرَهْ وَجُورْنَهْ وَبُنْدُقِيَّهْ وَجَنُوِيزَ وَسَائِرِ عَسَاكِرِ بَنِى الْأَصْفَرِ
sentences.tr: thumma aqbalati al-ifranju min sāʾiri aṭrāfihā kā al-far nasīsi wa-al-namsā wa-dūbarah wa-jūrnah wa-bundūqiyyah wa-janūyiza wa-sāʾiri ʿasākiri banī al-aṣfari
sentences.l: Then the Franks came on, from all their quarters — such as the French, and the Nimsā, and Dūbara, and Jūrna, and Venice, and Genoa — and the rest of the armies of the Sons of the Yellow.
sentences.i: Then the Franks came in from every side — the French, the Austrians, Dūbara, Jūrna, Venice, Genoa — and all the rest of the armies of the Banū al-Aṣfar.
sentences.n: The print splits al-Faransīs, “the French”, into three pieces (كا لفر نسيس), and the spacing is kept as printed. النمسا is Austria; بندقية and جنويز are Venice and Genoa; دوبره and جورنه are not identified. Banū al-Aṣfar, “sons of the yellow one”, is the Arabs’ old name for the Byzantines and, by extension, the peoples of Christian Europe.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا تَكَامَلَتِ الْعَسَاكِرُ وَضَاقَتْ بِهِمُ الْأَرْضُ مِنْ كَثْرَتِهِمْ أَمَرَهُمُ الْمَلِكُ الْأَكْبَرُ أَفْرِيدُونُ أَنْ يَرْحَلُوا عَنِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ فَرَحَلُوا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā takāmalati al-ʿasākiru wa-ḍāqat bihimu al-arḍu min kathratihim amarahumu al-maliku al-akbaru afrīdūnu an yarḥalū ʿani al-qusṭanṭīniyyati fa-raḥalū
sentences.l: And when the armies were complete, and the earth grew narrow with them from their multitude, the greatest king Afrīdūn commanded them to depart from Constantinople, and they departed.
sentences.i: When the armies were all together and the earth grew too narrow for them in their numbers, the Great King Afrīdūn ordered them to march out of Constantinople, and they marched.

sentences.t: وَاسْتَمَرَّ تَتَابُعُ عَسَاكِرِهِمْ فِى الرَّحِيلِ عَشَرَةَ أَيَّامٍ وَسَارُ وا حَتَّى نَزَلُوا بِوَادِي النُّعْمَانِ وَاسِعِ الْأَطْرَافِ وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ الْوَادِي قَرِيبًا مِنَ الْبَحْرِ الْمَالِحِ
sentences.tr: wa-istamarra tatābuʿu ʿasākirihim fī al-raḥīli ʿasharata ayyāmin wa-sārū ḥattā nazalū bi-wādī al-nuʿmāni wāsiʿi al-aṭrāfi wa-kāna dhālika al-wādī qarīban mina al-baḥri al-māliḥi
sentences.l: And the following of their armies one upon another in the departing continued ten days, and they went until they alighted in the valley of al-Nuʿmān, wide of reaches; and that valley was near the salt sea.
sentences.i: The armies went on streaming out for ten days, and they marched until they camped in a valley, the Valley of al-Nuʿmān, broad on every side, which lay near the salt sea.
sentences.n: The print splits سار وا (“they went”) into two pieces; the spacing is kept as printed. النعمان after وادي sits oddly beside the adjective that follows (perhaps a name that has intruded on the text); kept as printed and read as “the valley of al-Nuʿmān”. “The salt sea” is the Mediterranean.

sentences.t: فَأَقَامُوا ثَلْثَةَ أَيَّامٍ وَفِى الْيَوْمِ الرَّابِعِ أَرَادُوا أَنْ يَرْحَلُوا فَأَتَتْهُمُ الْأَخْبَارُ بِقُدُومِ عَسَاكِرِ الْإِسْلَامِ وَحُمَاةِ مِلَّةِ خَيْرِ الْأَنَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-aqāmū thalthata ayyāmin wa-fī al-yawmi al-rābiʿi arādū an yarḥalū fa-atathumu al-akhbāru bi-qudūmi ʿasākiri al-islāmi wa-ḥumāti millati khayri al-anāmi
sentences.l: And they stayed three days, and on the fourth day they wished to depart, and the news came to them of the coming of the armies of Islam, and the protectors of the community of the best of mankind.
sentences.i: They stayed there three days, and on the fourth they meant to move on, but word came that the armies of Islam were approaching — the defenders of the faith of the best of mankind.
sentences.n: “The best of mankind” is the Prophet Muḥammad. The print puts a damma on حماة, which is kept.

sentences.t: فَأَقَامُوا فِيهِ ثَلْثَةَ أَيَّامٍ أُخْرَى وَفِى الْيَوْمِ الرَّابِعِ رَأَوْا غُبَارًا طَارَحَتَّى سَدَّ الْأَقْطَارَ فَلَمْ تَمْضِ سَاعَةٌ مِنَ النَّهَارِ حَتَّى انْجَلَا ذَلِكَ الْغُبَارُ وَتَمَزَّقَ إِلَى الْجَوِّ وَطَارَ وَمَحَتْ ظُلْمَتَهُ كَوَاكِبُ الْأَسِنَّةِ وَالرِّمَاحِ وَبَرِيقُ بِيضِ الصِّفَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-aqāmū fīhi thalthata ayyāmin ukhrā wa-fī al-yawmi al-rābiʿi raʾaw ghubāran ṭāra ḥattā sadda al-aqṭāra fa-lam tamḍi sāʿatun mina al-nahāri ḥattā injalā dhālika al-ghubāru wa-tamazzaqa ilā al-jawwi wa-ṭāra wa-maḥat ẓulmatahu kawākibu al-asinnati wa-al-rimāḥi wa-barīqu bīḍi al-ṣifāḥi
sentences.l: So they stayed in it three days more, and on the fourth day they saw dust that flew until it blocked the regions; and an hour of the day had not passed until that dust cleared, and was torn apart into the air, and flew; and the stars of the spear-points and the lances and the gleam of the white broad-swords wiped out its darkness.
sentences.i: So they stayed there three days more, and on the fourth they saw a cloud of dust that rose until it shut out the horizons. Not an hour of the day had passed before the dust cleared and was torn apart into the air and blown away, and its darkness was wiped out by the stars of the spearheads and lances and the flash of bright broadswords.
sentences.n: The print runs طار and حتى together (طارحتى); the spacing is kept as printed. انجلا is the print’s spelling of انجلى.

sentences.t: وَبَانَ مِنْ تَحْتِهِ رَايَاتٌ إِسْلَامِيَّةٌ وَأَعْلَامٌ مُحَمَّدِيَّةٌ وَأَقْبَلَتِ الْفُرْسَانُ كَانْدِفَاعِ الْبِحَارِ فِي دُرُوعٍ تَحْسَبُهَا سُحُبًا مُزَرَّدَةً عَلَى أَقْمَارٍ
sentences.tr: wa-bāna min taḥtihi rāyātun islāmiyyatun wa-aʿlāmun muḥammadiyyatun wa-aqbalati al-fursānu ka-indifāʿi al-biḥāri fī durūʿin taḥsabuhā suḥuban muzarradatan ʿalā aqmārin
sentences.l: And there appeared from beneath it Islamic banners and Muḥammadan standards, and the horsemen came on like the rushing of the seas, in coats of mail that you would reckon clouds, ringed-with-mail, upon moons.
sentences.i: Beneath it appeared the banners of Islam and the standards of Muḥammad, and the horsemen came on like surging seas, in coats of mail that looked like clouds of linked rings above moons.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ تَقَابَلَ الْجَيْشَانِ وَالْتَطَمَ الْبَحْرَانِ وَوَقَعَتِ الْعَيْنُ فِى الْعَيْنِ فَأَوَّلُ مَنْ بَرَزَ لِلْقِتَالِ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ هُوَ وَعَسَاكِرُ الشَّامِ وَكَانُوا ثَلْثِينَ أَلْفَ عِنَانٍ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika taqābala al-jayshāni wa-iltaṭama al-baḥrāni wa-waqaʿati al-ʿaynu fī al-ʿayni fa-awwalu man baraza li-al-qitāli al-wazīru dandānu huwa wa-ʿasākiru al-shāmi wa-kānū thalthīna alfa ʿinānin
sentences.l: So at that the two armies faced each other, and the two seas dashed together, and the eye fell in the eye; and the first who came out to the fight was the vizier Dandān, he and the armies of Syria, and they were thirty thousand reins.
sentences.i: Then the two armies faced each other and the two seas crashed together, eye to eye, and the first to ride out to the fight was the vizier Dandān with the armies of Syria, thirty thousand riders.
sentences.n: The print has عمان (“Oman”) after ثلثين الف, a misprint for عنان, corrected here; “thousand reins” means riders. “The eye fell in the eye” is a stock phrase for two forces coming face to face.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ مَعَ الْوَزِيرِ مُقَدَّمُ التُّرْكِ وَمُقَدَّمُ الدَّيْلَمِ رُسْتُمُ وَبَهْرَامُ فِي عِشْرِينَ أَلْفَ فَارِسٍ وَطَلَعَ مِنْ وَرَائِهِمْ رِجَالٌ مِنْ صَوْبِ الْبَحْرِ الْمَالِحِ وَهُمْ لَابِسُونَ زَرَدَ الْحَدِيدِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna maʿa al-wazīri muqaddamu al-turki wa-muqaddamu al-daylami rustamu wa-bahrāmu fī ʿishrīna alfa fārisin wa-ṭalaʿa min warāʾihim rijālun min ṣawbi al-baḥri al-māliḥi wa-hum lābisūna zarada al-ḥadīdi
sentences.l: And with the vizier were the commander of the Turks and the commander of the Daylam, Rustam and Bahrām, with twenty thousand horsemen; and there came up behind them men from the direction of the salt sea, and they were wearing the chain-mail of iron,
sentences.i: With the vizier were the commander of the Turks and the commander of the Daylamites, Rustam and Bahrām, with twenty thousand horse; and behind them there came up men from the direction of the salt sea, wearing iron mail,
sentences.n: Bahrām is presumably the same man as the Turkish commander Bahramān named earlier in this night.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ صَارُوا فِيهِ كَالْبَدْرِ وَالسَّافِرَةِ فِي اللَّيَالِي الْعَاكِرَةِ وَصَارَتْ عَسَاكِرُ النَّصَارَى يُنَادُونَ يَالَعِيسَى وَمَرْيَمَ وَالصَّلِيبِ الْمُسَخَّمِ ثُمَّ انْطَبَقُوا عَلَى الْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ مِنْ عَسَاكِرِ الشَّامِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad ṣārū fīhi ka-al-badri wa-al-sāfirati fī al-layālī al-ʿākirati wa-ṣārat ʿasākiru al-naṣārā yunādūna yā la-ʿīsā wa-maryama wa-al-ṣalībi al-musakhkhami thumma inṭabaqū ʿalā al-wazīri dandāna wa-man maʿahu min ʿasākiri al-shāmi
sentences.l: and they had become in it like the full moon and the unveiled one in the murky nights; and the armies of the Christians began to call: O for ʿĪsā and Maryam and the blackened cross! Then they closed upon the vizier Dandān and those with him of the armies of Syria.
sentences.i: in which they shone like the full moon and the bare-faced stars on murky nights; and the Christian armies took up the cry, “For ʿĪsā and Maryam and the cross!” and then closed in upon the vizier Dandān and the Syrian troops with him.
sentences.n: The print has كالبد, a misprint for كالبدر, corrected here. Where it can be read, العاكرة means murky or turbid; the whole line is rhetorical and its images are only roughly clear. يالعيسى is يا لـ + عيسى, the lām of the battle-cry (“O for ʿĪsā!”), set as one word. المسخم, “blackened”, is the Muslim narrator’s insult for the cross.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ هَذَا كُلُّهُ بِتَدْبِيرِ الْعَجُوزِ ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي لِأَنَّ الْمَلِكَ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهَا قَبْلَ خُرُوجِهِ وَقَالَ لَهَا كَيْفَ الْعَمَلُ وَالتَّدْبِيرُ وَأَنْتِ السَّبَبُ فِي هَذَا الْأَمْرِ الْعَسِيرِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna hādhā kulluhu bi-tadbīri al-ʿajūzi dhāti al-dawāhī li-anna al-malika aqbala ʿalayhā qabla khurūjihi wa-qāla lahā kayfa al-ʿamalu wa-al-tadbīru wa-anti al-sababu fī hādhā al-amri al-ʿasīri
sentences.l: And all this was by the contrivance of the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī, because the king had turned to her before his going out, and said to her: How is the doing and the contriving, and you are the cause in this hard affair?
sentences.i: All this was by the scheming of the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī: before he set out the king had turned to her and said, “What are we to do, and how are we to plan? You are the cause of this hard business.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ اعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ الْكَبِيرُ وَالْكَاهِنُ الْخَطِيرُأَنِّي أُشِيرُ عَلَيْكَ بِأَمْرٍ يَعْجِزُ عَنْ تَدْبِيرِهِ إِبْلِيسُ وَلَوِ اسْتَعَانَ عَلَيْهِ بِحِزْبِهِ الْمَتَاعِيسِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati iʿlam ayyuhā al-maliku al-kabīru wa-al-kāhinu al-khaṭīru annī ushīru ʿalayka bi-amrin yaʿjizu ʿan tadbīrihi iblīsu wa-law istaʿāna ʿalayhi bi-ḥizbihi al-matāʿīsi
sentences.l: And she said: Know, O king the great and priest the weighty, that I counsel you with a matter that Iblīs is unable to contrive, even if he sought help against it with his party, the wretched ones.
sentences.i: She said: “Know, great king and mighty priest, that I advise you to a plan that even Iblīs could not devise, though he called on his whole wretched party to help him.”
sentences.n: The print runs الخطير and اني together (الخطيراني); the spacing is kept as printed. Iblīs is the devil; “his party” are his demons. The king of Rūm is addressed as both king and priest.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُ—بَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahra zāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula, as in every night; the print splits the name into شهر and زاد and breaks the last word with a dash.
